p: and drop thy word toward the: Speak sensibly, that all may understand.
righteous and the wicked: That is such which seem to have an outward show of righteousness by observation of the ceremonies of the law.
north: Meaning, through all the land.
heart: As though you were in extreme anguish.
For the tidings: Because of the great noise of the army of the Chaldeans.
glitter: And so cause fear.
rod of my son: Meaning, the sceptre showing that it will not spare the king, who would be as the son of God, and in his place.
as every tree: That is, the rest of the people.
slayer: That is, to the army of the Chaldeans.
smite therefore upon thy thigh: Read Eze 6:11.

and what if the sword despise: Ezekiel moved with compassion thus complains fearing the destruction of the kingdom which God had confirmed to David and his posterity by promise, which promise God performed although here it seemed to man's eye that it would utterly perish.
thy hands together: That is, encourage the sword.
one way or other: Provide for yourself: for you will see God's plague of all parts on this country.

two ways: This was spoken because when Nebuchadnezzar came against Judah his purpose was also to go against the Ammonites, but doubting in the way which enterprise to undertake first he consulted with his soothsayers and so went against Judah.
to Judah in Jerusalem the fortified: That is, to the tribe of Judah that kept themselves in Jerusalem.
the liver: He used conjuring and sorcery.
as a false divination in their: Because there was a league between the Jews and the Babylonians, they of Jerusalem will think nothing less than that this thing would come to pass.
but he will call to remembrance: That is, Nebuchadnezzar will remember the rebellion of Zedekiah, and so come on them.
prince of Israel: Meaning, Zedekiah who practised with the Egyptians to make himself high and able to resist the Babylonians.
diadem: Some refer this to the priest's attire: for Jehozadak the priest went into captivity with the king.

cometh whose right it is: That is, to the coming of Messiah: for though the Jews had some sign of government later under the Persians, Greeks and Romans, yet this restitution was not till Christ's coming and at length would be accomplished as was promised, Ge 49:10.

vanity to thee: Though the Jews and Ammonites would not believe that you, that is the sword, would come upon them, and said that the prophets who threatened spoke lies, yet you will as surely come as though you were already on their necks.
